svg.aria-label: Common fever and pain relievers: who can use them and how to use them safely. Doses follow the leaflet of the product you are using; dose children by body weight, with the measuring cup or tube supplied with the medicine; do not give medicine yourself to a baby under 3 months with a fever, go straight to a doctor; when danger signs appear, no medicine replaces seeing a doctor. 1, three common over-the-counter drugs: paracetamol (acetaminophen), adult 500 mg per dose, at least 4 hours apart, daily maximum 2000 mg, can be used in children from 3 months, first choice for fever in pregnancy (short term), no anti-inflammatory effect, main risk liver damage from overdose, better for people with stomach problems, a bleeding tendency, on anticoagulants, with kidney disease, dehydration or asthma; ibuprofen, adult 200-400 mg per dose, 4-6 hours apart, daily maximum 1200 mg, can be used in children from 6 months, avoid in pregnancy, especially after week 20, anti-inflammatory, main risks stomach bleeding and kidney harm, better for sprains, toothache, period pain and other pain with redness, swelling and inflammation; aspirin, as per the leaflet, not under 18, not in pregnancy, anti-inflammatory, main risks stomach bleeding, bleeding that will not stop and Reye's syndrome, not usually first choice for fever or pain, its most important use is to be chewed in a suspected heart attack. The adult doses are those commonly written on over-the-counter leaflets; higher doses only as a doctor directs. 2, shared rules: one drug at a time, do not combine or alternate them; read the ingredients first, many combination cold remedies contain paracetamol or aspirin, so count them in the total; wait the full interval, a fall of 1-1.5°C and feeling more comfortable means it is working, do not take an extra dose early because the temperature is not yet normal; write down the time and dose each time; for fever no more than 3 days, for pain no more than 5 days, then see a doctor if not better; no alcohol while taking paracetamol, people with liver disease or who drink heavily should ask a doctor first; lock all medicines away. 3, paracetamol overdose: for the first 1-2 days there may be no symptoms at all, or only nausea, vomiting, sweating and tiredness; only after 2-4 days do pain in the upper right abdomen, yellow skin or whites of the eyes, drowsiness or confusion appear, by which time the liver is already badly damaged; hospitals have a specific antidote, which works better the earlier it is given, best within 8 hours of taking the drug; if an overdose is possible, see a doctor at once, take the pack, note the time, do not induce vomiting, do not watch and wait at home. 4, see a doctor at once for: temperature of 40°C or more, high fever lasting more than 3 days, change in consciousness, seizures, difficulty breathing, severe headache and vomiting, pinpoint spots or bruises on the skin, a baby or toddler who is very listless; also see a doctor if a painkiller used as the leaflet says has not helped after 5 days
svg.title: Common fever and pain relievers: who can use them, and how to use them safely

g.text: Fever and pain relievers: who can use them, and how to use them safely
⚠ Doses follow the leaflet of the product you use. Dose children by body weight, using
the measuring cup or tube supplied with the medicine.

text.tspan: Baby under 3 months with a fever: don't give medicine yourself; see a doctor straight away.

g.text: When danger signs appear, no medicine replaces seeing a doctor.
① Choosing between three common over-the-counter drugs
* Usual adult dose on OTC leaflets; higher doses only as a doctor directs. Adults who drink heavily, or with liver
disease, malnutrition or body weight <50 kg, need a lower daily total: ask a doctor first
② Rules for all of them
1 One drug at a time: don't combine them, and don't “alternate” them
(it is easy to miscount the doses and the total)
2 Read the ingredients first: many combination cold remedies contain paracetamol (Chinese
names often include 氨酚, 酚麻 or 氨咖) or aspirin (listed as acetylsalicylic acid); count them
in the total. Already taking such a cold remedy? Don't add another fever reducer
3 Wait the full interval. A fall of 1-1.5°C and feeling better means it works; don't take
an extra dose early just because the temperature isn't back to normal
4 Write down the time and dose each time (especially when several people care for the patient)
5 Fever: no more than 3 days; pain: no more than 5 days. Still not better: see a doctor
6 No alcohol while taking paracetamol; lock all medicines away out of children's reach
③ Paracetamol overdose: often no early symptoms, so don't wait
best time to give the antidote
First 1-2 days: maybe no symptoms at all,
or only nausea, vomiting, sweating, tiredness
or whites of eyes, drowsiness or confusion
→ the liver is already badly damaged
Possible overdose? See a doctor at once: take the pack, count the tablets left,
note roughly when they were taken
✗ Don't induce vomiting ✗ Don't watch at home because there are “no symptoms now”
④ See a doctor at once for any of these (if possible)
High fever for more than 3 days
Pinpoint spots or bruises on the skin
A painkiller used as the leaflet says that hasn't helped after 5 days: see a doctor too
